items.summary: Korea has launched a comprehensive three-week inspection campaign targeting coastal fishing households that employ foreign seasonal workers, seeking to root out labor abuses and improve living standards in the country’s aging maritime sector. The joint crackdown, led by the Ministry of Justice and the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries, began Monday and will cover roughly 160 fishing households across the nation through Nov. 27. The initiative arrives amid growing scrutiny over the treatment of foreign laborers brought in to relieve severe workforce shortages in rural coastal communities. Officials said joint inspection teams — comprising government personnel, local authorities and civil rights groups — will directly visit five municipal regions with large seasonal worker allocations or lingering allegations of human rights violations. Local governments will independently audit an additional 22 municipalities. items.title: Seoul Station Plaza designated as no-drinking zone
items.title_zh: 首尔站广场被指定为禁酒区
items.summary: Seoul Station Plaza has been designated as a no-drinking zone starting Monday, officials said, amid concerns and complaints over homeless people drinking and causing discomfort to passersby. Seoul's Jung and Yongsan ward offices, which jointly oversee the area, announced that a total outdoor space of about 20,000 square meters around Seoul Station has been designated as an alcohol-free zone. Violators will be fined 50,000 won ($37) after a grace period ends on Feb. 28, officials said. The plaza has long been considered one of Seoul's main areas where homeless people gather and free meals are offered. Passersby have frequently complained about rowdy behavior by drinkers even during the daytime. During the grace period, local authorities plan to install directional signs and banners around the plaza while conducting on-site promotional campaigns to encourage voluntary public participation. Later Monday, officials from the ward offices, police and the national train operator Korea Railroad Corp. will jointly host a campaign and distribute leaflets to inform citizens of the new policy.

"The DPK pushed through the special counsel bill aimed at dropping charges against the president in just three days after forcibly ending the opposition party's filibuster through a vote. Lee made the pledge during a ceremony marking the 64th Day of Firefighting in the central city of Sejong, attended by government officials, firefighters, those who died while on duty and their bereaved families. The president stressed the ongoing climate crisis is increasing the diversity and scale of disasters, likely making them more complicated and difficult for firefighters to combat. "Preparing for and responding to changes a step ahead of time would be the way to protect the people's lives and ensure their safety," Lee said. He pledged to hire more firefighters, strengthen their command system and expand investment to enable them to respond more promptly and systematically to disasters and ensure public safety. items.summary: Leaders of the main opposition People Power Party (PPP) gathered outside Cheong Wa Dae on Monday to protest the recent passage of a bill calling for a special counsel investigation into alleged fabricated indictments targeting President Lee Jae Myung and others. The PPP leadership held a Supreme Council meeting outside the presidential office, after the ruling Democratic Party of Korea railroaded the bill through a plenary session of the National Assembly on Friday. The legislation calls for appointing an independent counsel to investigate suspicions the prosecution under former President Yoon Suk Yeol fabricated evidence or induced false testimonies to build cases against then opposition leader Lee and others. The PPP has denounced the effort as a pretext to cancel all of Lee's indictments, as his trials have been suspended under an article of the Constitution that exempts a sitting president from criminal prosecution except in cases of insurrection or treason. items.summary: Justice Minister nominee Lee Yong-cheol on Monday expressed reservations about nullifying indictments against President Lee Jae Myung following last week's passage of a special counsel bill to investigate allegations of fabricated indictments, including those that currently involve the president. The nominee, who currently serves as head of the Defense Acquisition Program Administration (DAPA), said the special counsel should focus exclusively on uncovering the truth. He was tapped Friday to become the justice minister, a post that has remained vacant for more than two months since Lee's first justice minister, Jung Sung-ho, resigned in late August. The National Assembly passed the special counsel bill on the same day amid protests from the main opposition People Power Party, which suspects the legislation is aimed at canceling all indictments against the president. The program combines the university’s traditional strengths in diplomacy, international trade and the humanities with emerging issues such as artificial intelligence (AI) and big data. In her lecture, titled “Changes in the International Order and Korea’s Diplomatic Choices,” Kim discussed the role and importance of diplomacy in the evolving international environment. She also introduced various programs and initiatives pursued by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and shared information to help students broaden their interest in international affairs and explore career opportunities in diplomacy. The university said it earned an overall score of 86.5 points in this year's survey, maintaining its top position in the category since 2014. It received particularly high scores in accuracy, friendliness and social value. The second-half survey covered 238 organizations across 58 general and platform service industries. The 2026 KS-SQI certification ceremony was held on Wednesday at the Grand Ballroom of Signiel Seoul in Lotte World Tower in southern Seoul. It drew about 200 attendees, including representatives of award-winning organizations. The KS-SQI is a service quality measurement model jointly developed by the KSA and Seoul National University’s Institute of Management Research. Designed to reflect the characteristics of Korea’s service industry and consumers, the index serves as a comprehensive measure of service quality nationwide. Marking its eighth edition, the Community Closet event, held twice a year in spring and autumn, is built around a simple but powerful principle: foreigners helping foreigners. Since 2023, the initiative has continued to grow, helping residents access essential items while encouraging a culture of sharing and reuse. Designed as a more dignified way to share, it is a free shopping event that allows foreign residents in need to receive donated clothes and household items in a welcoming environment. “For foreign residents navigating life in South Korea, finding a sense of belonging can be just as important as finding practical support," Katherine Ann Corteza, the center’s director, told The Korea Times. items.summary: Kwak Su-ryang, a professor in Kookmin University’s Department of Integrative Biotechnology, has been named to the 2026 World’s Top 2% Scientists list jointly released by Stanford University and Elsevier. The list recognizes the top 2 percent of researchers in their respective fields based on a comprehensive assessment of research performance, including citation metrics and publication output, using data from Elsevier’s Scopus database. Kwak’s research focuses on designing functional microorganisms and biomaterials using synthetic and computational biology, and evaluating their potential applications in precision medicine through multi-omics approaches. His notable achievements include a study published in Microbiome in 2020 that identified the effects of fecal microbiota transplantation on the gut microbiome and resistome, or the collection of antibiotic resistance genes in the human digestive system. items.title: Makkah Deputy Emir inaugurates Hajj Conference and Exhibition
items.title_zh: 麦加副埃米尔为朝觐会议和展览揭幕
items.summary: JEDDAH — Deputy Emir of Makkah Prince Saud bin Mishaal inaugurated on Sunday the sixth edition of the Hajj Conference and Exhibition at Jeddah Superdome. The four-day event is being held under the patronage of Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques King Salman. The conference, with the theme "From Makkah to the World," is organized by the Ministry of Hajj and Umrah in cooperation with the Pilgrim Experience Program. The inaugural ceremony was attended by several senior Saudi officials, heads of Hajj missions, and representatives of Hajj affairs offices from various countries of the Islamic world. The Deputy Emir of Makkah toured the accompanying exhibition, where he viewed the latest technologies, enriching initiatives, and smart solutions designed to enhance services for pilgrims. He also visited the pavilions of participating entities representing the governmental, private, and non-profit sectors. In his address on behalf of King Salman, Prince Saud welcomed the attendees to their second home, the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, and conveyed the King's greetings.“With God's help and guidance, Saudi Arabia continues its blessed efforts to serve the Two Holy Mosques and pilgrims, placing this noble mission at the forefront of its priorities. The Kingdom reaffirms its commitment to the continuous development of the Hajj system, enhancing service quality, harnessing the latest technologies, and strengthening integration among government agencies to facilitate the pilgrim's journey from departure until a safe return. The continued success of Hajj seasons stands as a testament to the readiness and high efficiency of the Hajj system,” the deputy emir said, adding, the Hajj and Umrah Conference and Exhibition is one of the key enablers of this success, contributing to enhanced cooperation and joint coordination, the conclusion of agreements, and improved preparedness for the Hajj season. Speaking on the occasion, Minister of Hajj and Umrah Dr. Tawfiq Al-Rabiah highlighted the most significant transformations in the Hajj and Umrah system. These included fostering competition, increasing the number of companies providing services to pilgrims from abroad to 34, expanding direct contracting to 58 countries, and extending Hajj access to pilgrims from an additional 75 countries through the Direct Hajj Program. He also highlighted early preparations for the 1448 AH Hajj season in coordination with Hajj affairs offices in 78 countries, alongside the development of the holy sites and transportation infrastructure. Dr. Al-Rabiah also highlighted the digital transformation that has driven the number of users of the “Nusk” platform and application to more than 70 million. He noted that the Hajj satisfaction rate reached 93 percent in 1447 AH, emphasizing that the Hajj Conference and Exhibition has evolved into a global platform for early preparations, forging partnerships, finalizing contracts, and advancing services. The opening ceremony also featured an address on behalf of the heads of Hajj affairs offices, delivered by Minister of Hajj and Umrah of Indonesia Dr. Muhammad Irfan Yusuf. It also witnessed the launch of the Awareness and Training Forum and the Unified Staff Portal. During the ceremony, the Deputy Emir witnessed the signing of eight agreements and memoranda of understanding. The exhibition, with participation and attendance from over 150 countries, spreads over 67,000 square meters and features more than 15 major zones and programs covering operations, knowledge exchange, technology, business, innovation, awareness, and training.

items.title: US-Saudi Business Council charts new path to boost trade, investment and economic ties
items.title_zh: 美国-沙特商业理事会为促进贸易、投资和经济关系开辟了新途径
items.summary: WASHINGTON — The meeting of the Board of Directors of the U.S.- Saudi Business Council reaffirmed its commitment to supporting the strategic and economic partnership between the two countries. The board expressed confidence in the council’s strength and continued growth potential. The meeting also reviewed priorities for expanding trade between the two countries, stimulating investment, and strengthening business cooperation in sectors of mutual interest. Saudi Minister of Energy, Industry and Mineral Resources Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman and Minister of Investment Fahad Al-Saif, along with several senior business leaders from Saudi Arabia and the United States attended the meeting, which was co-chaired by the Saudi-U.S. Business Council’s Co-Chair Persons Lubna Olayan and Jane Fraser. During the meeting, Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman reaffirmed Saudi Arabia’s commitment to energy security and industrial development. He highlighted emerging opportunities in artificial intelligence and critical infrastructure and underscored the strength of the partnership between the Saudi and U.S. business sectors.For his part, Minister Al-Saif outlined the key features of the upcoming second edition of the National Investment Strategy. He indicated that it aims to shift the focus from promoting investment to turning investment opportunities into actual investments, thereby accelerating economic growth.The ministers discussed key priorities and opportunities for deepening cooperation between the two countries with council leaders. They underscored the importance of trade relations between the two countries and the council’s role in developing them.Olayan said the business community remained focused on future opportunities despite the challenges facing the region, highlighting the long history of successful trade partnership between Saudi Arabia and the U.S. and the potential to deepen it. She noted that strengthening communication between executive leaders would open up new avenues for investment, innovation, and economic growth in both countries.Fraser said the meeting reflected the commitment of business leaders in both countries to working together to support economic growth and expand opportunities. She also highlighted the council’s role in strengthening ties, stimulating investment, and supporting shared prosperity.The board members discussed the council’s work program, which aims to identify and address structural barriers to trade and investment between the two countries, develop practical and actionable recommendations, and deepen cooperation with government entities and private-sector institutions in both countries.The discussions also covered emerging strategic opportunities to accelerate trade cooperation and facilitate partnerships in priority sectors. These efforts are part of a work program focused on expanding trade, unlocking investment opportunities, and strengthening ties between Saudi and U.S. companies and institutions.In light of the current regional challenges, the council stressed the importance of maintaining communication and close cooperation between the two countries and ensuring the continuity of institutional work. It affirmed that economic relations between the two countries are built on solid foundations and that the private sector plays a key role in developing them.U.S.- Saudi Business Council CEO Charles Hallab said the board members’ expertise and commitment reflected the importance of Saudi-U.S. economic relations and the scale of available opportunities. He stressed the council’s commitment to translating confidence in the partnership into practical action to address obstacles, open up new areas for business and investment, and serve shared economic interests.The council reaffirmed its commitment to continuing to work with public- and private-sector leaders to strengthen the foundations of economic cooperation between the two countries. It will draw on the expertise of its board members and the global presence of their institutions to support a new phase of institutional engagement and communication between the two business communities.Established in 1993 under a Saudi royal decree and a U.S. executive action, the Saudi-U.S. Business Council works to promote business, trade, and investment between the two countries. It brings together business leaders and government entities to develop trade cooperation priorities, unlock investment opportunities, and address issues affecting trade and business flows.

items.title: NCM: Al-Jumum records highest rainfall at 24.1 mm Saturday
items.title_zh: NCM ：周六Al-Jumum记录的最高降雨量为24.1毫米
items.summary: JEDDAH — Al-Jumum governorate in the Makkah region recorded the Kingdom's highest rainfall on Saturday at 24.1 mm, and it was followed by Al-Madain in the Hail region at 23.2 mm, according to data released by the National Center for Meteorology (NCM).Jeddah Islamic Port recorded 20.6 mm, Badr governorate 13.6 mm, Unaizah governorate 6.5 mm, and Al-Qaisumah Airport 3.1 mm, the center said. Several regions of Saudi Arabia recorded moderate to heavy rain on Saturday.

items.title: Coalition: Ballistic missile launchers destroyed in Saada and Sanaa
items.title_zh: 联盟：萨达和萨那的弹道导弹发射器被摧毁
items.summary: RIYADH — Maj. Gen. Turki Al-Maliki, spokesperson of the Coalition to Restore Legitimacy in Yemen, said that two ballistic missile launchers, used by the terrorist Houthi militia, in an attempted attack on Riyadh on Sunday were destroyed in Saada. He said that another ballistic missile launcher, used by the Houthi militia in an attempted attack on the Eastern Province on Sunday, was destroyed in Sanaa.

items.title: Saudi foreign minister arrives in Paris to attend G7 ministerial meeting
items.title_zh: 沙特外长抵达巴黎出席七国集团部长级会议
items.summary: PARIS — Minister of Foreign Affairs Prince Faisal bin Farhan arrived in Paris on Sunday to attend the G7 Foreign Ministers’ Meeting, hosted by France on November 9 and 10 at the invitation of the French G7 Presidency.The meeting will discuss key international developments and issues, as well as efforts to resolve crises and conflicts, maritime and port security, combating smuggling, enhancing the effectiveness of humanitarian response, food security and nutrition, and artificial intelligence security.Saudi Arabia’s participation in the meeting reflects its active role in France’s G7 Presidency and its commitment to strengthening consultation and coordination with international partners and intensifying joint efforts to address current regional and international challenges.

items.title: Al-Samaani: Courts of Appeal a vital safeguard for justice and judicial integrity
items.title_zh: 萨马尼：上诉法院是正义和司法廉正的重要保障
items.summary: RIYADH — Minister of Justice Walid Al-Samaani underscored the pivotal role of Courts of Appeal as the second tier of the judicial system. He described them as a vital safeguard for justice, ensuring thorough judicial scrutiny of judgments and proper consideration of appeals, thereby strengthening judicial oversight and enhancing the quality, integrity, and efficiency of judicial proceedings. Addressing a meeting with the heads of judicial circuits at the Court of Appeal in Riyadh, the minister affirmed that progress in the justice sector has been achieved through the unlimited support of Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques King Salman and the continued support and follow-up of Crown Prince and Prime Minister Mohammed bin Salman. Al-Samaani commended improvements in the performance of Courts of Appeal. He emphasized the important role of circuit heads in overseeing the quality of judicial work, ensuring that judgments are properly reasoned, addressing grounds for appeal and substantive arguments, and resolving cases in ways that improve procedural efficiency and the beneficiary experience throughout the stages of litigation. The minister also outlined future directions for advancing judicial work, including strengthening the role of technical offices and expanding the use of artificial intelligence applications to support the preparation of studies and draft judgments. He also emphasized the need to enhance the beneficiary experience, thereby fostering greater institutional maturity and elevating the overall quality of judicial services.

items.title: Saudi Arabia offers condolences to Egypt over fatal train collision
items.title_zh: 沙特阿拉伯就火车相撞事故向埃及表示哀悼
items.summary: RIYADH — Saudi Arabia expressed its deep condolences and sincere sympathies to Egypt and the families of the deceased following the Al-Ayyat train accident on the Cairo–Aswan agricultural road in Giza Governorate.In a statement, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs expressed on Sunday Saudi Arabia’s solidarity with the government and people of Egypt following this tragic accident, wishing those injured a speedy recovery. At least seven people have been killed and more than 100 injured after two trains collided between Kafr Ammar and Al-Raqqa stations in Giza, which is close to the capital, Cairo in Egypt. Several train carriages were derailed after a train collided with the rear of another train, according to the Egyptian National Railways Authority.

items.title: GCC railway to begin full operations by December 2030 as member states sign landmark agreement
items.title_zh: 随着成员国签署具有里程碑意义的协议，海湾合作委员会铁路将于2030年12月开始全面运营
items.summary: MANAMA — The Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) railway project is scheduled to become fully operational by December 2030, with overall completion reaching 55.92%, as member states signed a landmark agreement Sunday to establish an integrated railway network connecting the six Gulf countries.The General Agreement for the GCC Railway Project was signed at Riffa Al Zahir Palace in Bahrain under the patronage and in the presence of Bahraini Crown Prince and Prime Minister Prince Salman bin Hamad Al Khalifa.The signing ceremony was attended by GCC Secretary-General Jasem Albudaiwi and the transport and communications ministers of the member states.According to the GCC General Secretariat, the project has achieved an overall completion rate of 55.92%, with December 2030 set as the target for full operation.The agreement establishes a common framework governing the commitments of member states, coordinating implementation and operational activities, and ensuring integration among their national railway networks.It represents a major milestone in the development of a unified Gulf transportation system designed to facilitate passenger and freight movement across the region.Speaking on the occasion, Albudaiwi said the agreement marked a significant step toward strengthening Gulf integration in the transportation sector and establishing a coordinated railway system across GCC countries."The General Agreement for the GCC Railway Project represents a significant step in bolstering Gulf integration in the transport sector and regulating the railway transport system within the GCC states," he said.He added that the agreement would support the operation of a railway network linking all GCC member states through a single, integrated and interoperable regional system, strengthening connectivity and facilitating transportation among member countries.The project aims to provide safe, reliable, economical and environmentally friendly transportation services for passengers and freight, operating under common technical specifications and approved safety and sustainability standards.It is also expected to strengthen intra-GCC trade by connecting economic and industrial centers with ports and logistics hubs, improving the competitiveness of Gulf economies.Albudaiwi expressed appreciation to Bahrain's King Hamad bin Isa Al Khalifa, who chairs the current session of the GCC Supreme Council, and the leaders of GCC member states for their continued support of joint Gulf initiatives and strategic development projects.The secretary-general praised the efforts of the relevant teams across GCC member states and the GCC Railways Authority in advancing the project.He emphasized that the railway network would contribute to economic development, create employment and investment opportunities, and strengthen economic and social ties among Gulf communities.

items.title: Saudi students set record with over 37,000 research projects in National Gifted Olympiad
items.title_zh: 沙特学生在国家天才奥林匹克竞赛中创下超过37,000个研究项目的纪录
items.summary: RIYADH — The King Abdulaziz and His Companions Foundation for Giftedness and Creativity (Mawhiba) and the Ministry of Education announced that more than 37,000 research projects had been submitted by male and female students across Saudi Arabia to the Research Track "Ibdaa" of the National Gifted Olympiad 2027. This marks a record number in the competition’s history, representing a 7.83 percent increase compared with last year. Mawhiba said the number of registered research projects reached 37,008, surpassing last year’s total of 34,321 by 2,687 projects. This reflects growing student interest in scientific research and innovation, following the previous edition, Ibdaa 2026, which set a world record recognized by Guinness World Records. The registered student projects have advanced to the electronic judging stage, which runs until November 16. This will be followed by online judging interviews and the announcement of projects shortlisted for the central exhibitions scheduled for December, leading up to the National Gifted Olympiad finals in January 2027. The National Gifted Olympiad, organized by Mawhiba in partnership with the Ministry of Education, aims to identify and nurture gifted students, develop their scientific, research, and innovation capabilities, and prepare them to compete in international science Olympiads and exhibitions. It also seeks to develop national talent capable of contributing to the knowledge economy and achieving the objectives of Saudi Vision 2030.

items.title: High tech services for pilgrims showcased as Hajj Conference and Exhibition kicks off in Jeddah
items.title_zh: 随着朝觐会议和展览在吉达拉开帷幕，为朝圣者提供高科技服务
items.summary: JEDDAH — The sixth edition of the Hajj Conference and Exhibition opened on Sunday at Jeddah Superdome, bringing together more than 520 entities from the government, private and non-profit sectors from within Saudi Arabia and abroad. Organized by the Ministry of Hajj and Umrah in cooperation with the Pilgrim Experience Program, a Saudi Vision 2030 program, the four-day event is being held under the theme "From Makkah to the World," reflecting the Saudi leadership's continued commitment to serving pilgrims. The exhibition, with participation and attendance from over 150 countries, would cover more than 67,000 square meters and feature more than 15 major zones and programs covering operations, knowledge exchange, technology, business, innovation, awareness, and training. The conference is part of early preparations for the Hajj season of 2027, bringing together Hajj affairs offices, service providers, and relevant authorities to finalize procedures, arrangements, and contracts; explore available services and solutions for the upcoming season; and discuss ways to enhance readiness and improve services for pilgrims.The conference program is organized around three main tracks: infrastructure and operational services; empowerment and integration; and development and sustainability. The event showcases services and solutions across transportation, accommodation, catering, healthcare and technology, highlighting some of the arrangements that begin several months before the arrival of the pilgrims in Saudi Arabia. These day-to-day details offer a glimpse into the pilgrim’s journey before arrival, bringing together travel, aviation, accommodation, catering and healthcare services. The exhibition enables participating entities to learn about one another’s needs and explore opportunities for cooperation, while the business center provides a setting for professional meetings, contract finalization, and agreement signing. The innovation and technology spaces bring together innovators and service providers, linking proposed solutions to the actual challenges encountered during the pilgrim’s journey. The exhibition also features training and qualification programs to enhance staff readiness and their ability to deliver services. The event provides a platform for innovators to connect with the entities responsible for developing and operating Hajj services, opening up opportunities to address pilgrims’ needs while traveling and provide them with information at different stages of their journey. The Innovation Zone, the hackathon and the Technology Oasis bring together field experience and the expertise of innovators, entrepreneurs and technology companies to examine challenges and showcase solutions that address pilgrims' needs. These encounters allow ideas to be tested in their intended operating environments, while direct engagement with service providers helps innovators understand operational requirements and explore opportunities to deploy technologies and digital solutions to improve the pilgrim journey, from planning crowd movements to facilitating access to information and services. These spaces form part of a broader conference approach that links innovation to real needs and strengthens cooperation among researchers, technology specialists, and service providers, supporting the development of solutions that address real-world challenges facing the Hajj ecosystem.By bringing together challenges identified by field workers and ideas put forward by innovators, the exhibition offers an opportunity to build partnerships that turn knowledge and technology into services pilgrims can experience through a smoother, higher-quality journey.
